To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aging process is characterized by increased sensitivity to inflammatory stimuli, which is caused by up-regulation of neutral sphingmyelinase 2 and accumulation of ceramide, and that these changes can be reversed by calorie restriction.

(i) the activity of neutral sphingomylines is increased in aging and (ii) the increase in NSMase2 activity is linked to oxidative stress and is responsible for the IL-1beta hyperresponsiveness in aging.

the aging-associated increase in the activity of nSMase-2 in liver is caused by the decline in GSH content and that the increased activity of nsmase2 in aging underlies hepatic IL- 1b hyperresponsivness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of nSMases and ceramide in aging and inflammatory stress, and with developing strategies to prevent and/or treat aging and inflammation.
elucidating the mechanisms of aging-associated changes in cellular responses to inflammatory stress and the role of nSMase in this process.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the activity of nSMase and how these mechanisms are altered during aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nSMase2 is a key mediator of aging and aging-related diseases, and its regulation is intimately linked to cellular redox status.

aging is accompanied by a decline in the activity of nSMase1, which is compensated by an increase in nSMase2 activity and this change in nSMase expression and function contributes to the aging-associated pro-inflammatory state.
the aging process in liver involves an increase in the expression of nSMase-2 and its associated signaling pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nSMase2 is the major mediator of IL-1beta-induced responses in the liver and its activity is regulated by oxidative stress.
nSMase2 is a key player in cellular responses to cytokines, and that the aging-associated increase in nSMase activity contributes to the development of an "inflamm-aging" phenotype in the liver.
aging is accompanied by a decline in cellular antioxidant capacity and an increase in oxidative stress, which in turn results in increased activity of neutral SMase and the accumulation of ceramide.
The main takeaway from our work is that

nSMase2 is a key regulator of the aging-associated pro-inflammatory state and that the decline in the GSH content in liver plays a critical role in the aging-associated increase in the nSMase2 activity and function.
aging is associated with a decline in the cellular antioxidant capacity, leading to an increased susceptibility to inflammatory stress and to the onset of a pro-inflammatory state in the elderly.
aging is characterized by a decline in GSH content and an increased activity of nSMPD2, which in turn leads to an increased sensitivity to pro-inflammatory stimuli, such as TNFalpha and IL-1beta.
